feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy-heavy roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and dense, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at the same organization show growth, trust, and increasing leadership scope.  
- Good impact signals: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms make achievements believable.  
- Strong positioning: the summary, competencies, and technical stack consistently support a senior digital strategy/communications brand.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Soft Skills” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Add more outcome-focused results: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more quantified business/communications outcomes would increase impact.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; use serial commas consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); “front-end”/hyphenation and date formats should be standardized. “Coleman DAVIS” is also stylistically inconsistent unless intentional branding.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns with the CV’s senior digital leadership profile. It would be sharper with a more specific opening, cleaner phrasing, and less overlap with the competencies and experience sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard CV style.
- Lead with your level and niche: “Digital communications and strategy leader” or “Digital strategy and communications lead.”
- Add one or two high-value differentiators from recent roles, such as enterprise web modernization, analytics/governance, or mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Tighten the final sentence to reduce generic phrasing and improve flow.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, enterprise web modernization, editorial workflows, and digital governance. Strong track record in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language repeat heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership/strategy capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Digital transformation strategy” instead of “Digital strategy & transformation,” “Editorial systems & governance” instead of “Editorial workflow design.”
- Group related items and reduce overlap: Digital transformation strategy • Web platform & CMS leadership • Editorial systems & governance • Cross-channel communications • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder alignment • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia production
- Standardize style: use either all nouns/phrases or all “-ing” forms; avoid mixing “communication,” “administration,” and “design.”
- Consider dropping “multi-channel communication” in favor of “Cross-channel communications leadership” to better match seniority.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, cross-channel communications, analytics, and advocacy messaging.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also repeats Soft Skills almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Make it sharper by foregrounding scope, platform leadership, and 1–2 concrete outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter summary line: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements across web, campaigns, content operations, and AI-enabled search.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with strong verbs: “Built,” “Led,” “Developed,” “Advised.”
- Add measurable scope where possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing teams supported, workflow time saved, search/discovery improvements.
- Example phrasing: “Led development of an AI-enabled search experience, defining retrieval strategy, structured content workflows, and discovery UX for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement” repeats themes already covered in the headline and competencies.
- Drupal microsite and AI search details overlap with “Recent Projects”; keep this entry focused on role-level impact, not project descriptions.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to foreground outcomes and distinguish strategic leadership from execution covered in earlier NACo roles. Emphasize enterprise impact, team leadership, and modernization results.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to lead with outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: team size, budget, reporting cadence, production volume, engagement growth, efficiency gains, or reduced reliance on vendors after building the studio.
- Tighten channel bullet: replace “reaching tens of thousands / serving thousands” with exact subscriber/follower counts or strongest engagement/result metric.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Video production and recurring advocacy content overlap with the Associate Communications Director and Digital Media Manager roles; keep this entry focused on building the in-house studio and scaling organizational capacity.
- “Governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning” may overlap with consultant/topline language; make it specific to NACo systems or outcomes.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Tighten it to emphasize scope you owned at this level and any measurable growth in newsletters, video, or workflow efficiency.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add outcomes where possible: newsletter open/click rates, audience growth, video cadence/views, or workflow improvements (e.g., faster publishing, fewer bottlenecks).
- Combine the last two bullets for concision: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with both the footer project and the 2015–2018 role; frame this here as scaling/operationalizing the series rather than launching it.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strategically in the 2022–2024 Director entry.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize leadership scope and strategic value, not generic skill labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, differentiated wording, e.g.:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy content strategy
- Audience-centered content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “content strategy” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- Keep terminology parallel: all noun phrases, all leadership/strategy-oriented.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this section to scale from recent roles rather than here (10,000+ pages, 50+ publishers, 3.5M annual page views).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” overlaps with multiple work-experience bullets on storytelling, editorial planning, and campaign development.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills item, tighten it around higher-value, recent capabilities and group tools under outcomes-oriented labels.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped, impact-oriented phrases rather than a long tool list:
- Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages
- CMS modernization & front-end implementation
- API integrations & workflow automation
- Airtable-based operational systems
- AI-enabled search & discovery experiences
- Replace “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” with “front-end implementation” unless the target role explicitly requires coding keywords.
- Put the most relevant/recent strengths first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- If space allows, use “search & discovery” instead of just “search experiences” to sound more user- and outcome-focused.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and less tool-by-tool.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search” already echo Core Competencies, so avoid repeating identical phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capability and decision impact, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & performance optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” rather than eight separate fragments.
- Replace weaker phrases like “Leadership reporting” with stronger business language such as “executive reporting” or “decision-ready dashboards.”
- Consider: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive dashboards and reporting • SEO, UX and performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is highly duplicative of “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool stack.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact framing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize operational leadership and production scope rather than listing basic capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level bullets:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production  
- Livestream and hybrid event production  
- PTZ camera and in-house studio operations  
- Run-of-show, technical coordination and live delivery
- If you can support it elsewhere, add scale/context in adjacent experience bullets instead of here (e.g., studio built, recurring video series, event support volume).
- Keep wording leadership-oriented; avoid “editing” alone if the CV is targeting senior digital/platform roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production” and “livestream operations” already appear in Core Competencies; consider simplifying one section to avoid repetition.
- Tool-specific detail is better left to “Technical + IT” (e.g., Premiere Pro, Audition).

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or reframed to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize the most relevant/recent tools: lead with Drupal, then WordPress and SharePoint; move GitHub Pages last or remove if lightly used.
- Consider adding proficiency context: “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, align wording to recent impact: “Drupal CMS modernization • WordPress • SharePoint intranet/collaboration • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Keep it concise and platform-focused; avoid repeating broader “CMS modernization” language already covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2], which already lists the same platforms plus technical capabilities.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor beside enterprise platforms unless supported by project/work experience.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use in recent roles and group items more clearly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Technical integrations: APIs, Google Tag Manager • Deployment/automation: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) if space is tight; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner and equally credible.
- Consider replacing broad terms with stronger phrasing: “API integrations” → “REST/API integrations”; “GitHub Actions” → “CI/CD automation” if that better reflects actual use.
- If you can substantiate it elsewhere, add scope or outcome in adjacent experience bullets rather than here (e.g., implemented GTM, automated deployments, built edge/serverless functions).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may overlap with GitHub Actions unless differentiated as dev/deployment automation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more clearly organized.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function to improve scanability: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Consider renaming to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” to better match the actual mix of tools.
- Keep only tools you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if Airtable/Power Automate/Zapier are strongest, place them first.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie 1–2 tools to outcomes in recent experience bullets rather than expanding this list here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language verbatim.
- Slack/Teams are low-signal unless central to systems design; consider dropping one or both if space is tight.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platforms, but this item is too bare and reads like a generic software list. It should signal level/relevance without repeating the strong email leadership already shown in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency and standardize naming: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show applied use, e.g. **newsletter operations, audience segmentation, journey/campaign execution**
- Example rewrite: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Mailchimp (newsletter operations, audience segmentation, campaign automation)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding claims like “managed newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in Work Experience.
- Don’t repeat broad “multi-channel communications” language already covered in Core Competencies and recent roles.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content execution, and any concrete outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: website size/traffic at the time, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience growth, or turnaround/time-saved from workflow improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; replace with specifics such as “supported website refresh,” “produced weekly video briefings,” and “managed livestream production.”
- Consider: “Supported NACo’s website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Workflow and cross-channel coordination also appear in later NACo roles; keep this entry focused on foundational setup and hands-on production.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the unique achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with clearer business support language: “Supported innovation and research initiatives that informed county-focused programs and policy communications.”
- Keep multimedia mention concise and secondary: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support organizational campaigns and program priorities.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of episodes, audiences reached, projects supported, or types of policy/program deliverables.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on podcast launch and research/program support.
- Avoid broad claims about digital leadership here, since stronger, more recent evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.
